name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with a PVI of R+28
Incumbent Josh Brecheen running for reelection with a large financial edge
Democratic challenger Brandon Wade raised only about $4,300 with $86 on hand
Prediction markets price Brecheen at roughly 98% to win
model.rationale: This is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, and the incumbent holds every structural advantage: incumbency, a dominant fundraising position, and a challenger with essentially no resources. Prediction markets and the fundamentals both point to an overwhelming Republican win, so the forecast stays close to the baseline with no evidence favoring an upset.
model.watch: The race is unlikely to move; only a major unforeseen scandal or the emergence of a well-funded Democratic challenger would warrant reevaluation.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District is a heavily Republican seat in the state's southeastern region, and first-term Republican Josh Brecheen is seeking reelection with the full weight of the district's partisan lean behind him. His Democratic opponent, Brandon Wade, has raised only a few thousand dollars and reported just $86 on hand, with no outside spending on either side. An independent candidate, Ronnie Hopkins, is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Brecheen roughly a 98% chance of winning. With a Republican partisan index of about +28 and an incumbent facing an unfunded challenger, the race is rated Safe Republican, with the only real question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
